cf:fighter-opening-stop.why: the second sentence of the fighter's opportunity-attack feature is that an enemy hit by one stops moving if a move provoked it. movement.walk asks can_move once, before the first step, and never again, so immobilising the mover inside the opportunity window leaves it walking the rest of its path. Verified: a creature immobilised on its first step still covered all five squares. cf:fighter-opening writes the attack bonus half (stop a move that is in progress)

cf:fighter-talent-rest.wants: legs in chargen.BUILDS["fighter"] for the talents the two it has do not mean, plus c.proficiency and a free-hand / off-hand grip on Gear
cf:fighter-talent-rest.why: the class page prints six talents and chargen.BUILDS["fighter"] carries two legs. cf:fighter-grip writes the two that are the legs -- the one-handed and two-handed weapon talents. The other four have no leg: one turns unproficient weapons into improvised ones and adds an AC bonus out of heavy armour, one pays temporary hit points on every melee or close hit, one wants a weapon in one hand and the other hand empty or grabbing, and one keys off a second weapon with the off-hand property. Gear records what is held but not what a hand is free for, and nothing models proficiency as a thing a feature can grant

cf:ranger-style.wants: a feat model -- feats on a character and c.feat(...)
cf:ranger-style.why: the class page prints five styles and chargen.BUILDS["ranger"] carries two legs. The two legs that do match are the two whose entire printed content is a granted feat, and nothing in the engine is a feat -- the remaining clause of one of them is an off-hand rule Gear.two_weapon already makes true. The three styles that do carry mechanics (a speed bonus while unencumbered, an AC bonus against openings a ranged attack provokes, a companion) have no leg to be gated on, and the companion one is blocked twice over -- see p10594 (to read one -- plus legs in chargen.BUILDS["ranger"] for the styles that carry mechanics)

cf:rogue-tactic-club.wants: chargen.BUILDS["rogue"] to carry a third leg, plus Keyword.RATTLING
cf:rogue-tactic-club.why: one of the four printed tactics grants proficiency with two weapon groups, lets those groups stand in for the light blade cf:rogue-bonus requires, and adds a Strength rider to attacks carrying a keyword the enum does not have. cf:rogue-tactic writes the two legs the class's two builds can carry; this one has no leg to ask about and its payload is blocked on the same keyword as p10740 and p4499

cf:rogue-tactic-stealth.wants: chargen.BUILDS["rogue"] to carry a fourth leg, plus c.check(skill, dc)
cf:rogue-tactic-stealth.why: one of the four printed tactics is entirely penalties to Stealth checks for moving and running, and a check to go unseen after moving 3 squares. The engine rolls no skill checks -- the same hold as m2963a4 -- and the class has two builds, so there is neither a leg to gate it on nor a check to modify

cf:warlord-archer.why: it grants proficiency with a weapon group and lets a ranged basic attack with a bow use Strength for the attack and damage rolls instead of Dexterity. basic.RANGED declares its ability in the header and nothing can rewrite it for one creature. Neither warlord leg in chargen.BUILDS carries a bow either, so there would be nothing to shoot with (name which ability a basic attack uses)

cf:warlord-initiative.why: its whole printed content is a +2 power bonus to initiative for the warlord and every ally within 10 squares who can see and hear it. Initiative.bonus is read once, inside _roll_initiative, and Encounter.start rolls initiative *before* _arm_traits -- so a trait cannot reach the only roll it exists to change, and there is no modifier key for it either (applied before Encounter._roll_initiative)

cf:warlord-presence.wants: action points -- a pool on the character, spending one as an action, and an event announcing it
cf:warlord-presence.why: every one of its six printed options fires when an ally spends an action point for an extra action. Nothing in the engine has an action point, which is the same wall p2593, p7448 and the level 6 and 7 warlord rows hit. Two of the six -- the Charisma one and the Intelligence one -- would map cleanly onto the two warlord legs once there is an event to hang them from

cf:warlord-shield.wants: p10887 in the tree, plus a leg in chargen.BUILDS["warlord"] for it
cf:warlord-shield.why: one of three mutually exclusive leader features. Its content is proficiency with a shield -- not a thing a feature can grant -- and gaining one named power, which c.grant_row could hand over except that the power is not declared anywhere. cf:warlord-senses writes the one of the three whose content is purely narrative

cf:wizard-implement-rest.why: a wizard class feature about its familiar, which no row creates

cf:wizard-spellbook.wants: a spellbook -- powers a character owns but has not prepared
cf:wizard-spellbook.why: the whole feature is holding two dailies and two utilities per slot and preparing one of each after a rest. Powers holds only what is known, so owning an unprepared power cannot be said and neither can preparing one. Same missing thing as p7377

m2963a4.why: its whole content is 'any character can make a DC 25 History check as a minor action', and on a success the m2963 gains vulnerable 10 to that character's next attack. The engine rolls no skill checks and holds no DCs, and the row is spent by a creature that does not own it, which `use` has no door for -- so both halves of the sentence are unsayable, not just the number

m3062a2.why: the rusting item is destroyed; nothing removes gear from a creature

m3064a2.why: its whole Hit is 'the decaying magic item is destroyed', and it can only target a creature carrying one; nothing removes gear from a creature and Gear records no enhancement bonus to have been decayed. Same sentence as m3062a2

m3064a3.why: its whole Effect is reducing the enhancement bonus of the weapon or implement that hit it, to a minimum of 0, until the end of the encounter; Weapon has no enhancement bonus and Gear has no armour object, so there is no number to reduce

m4853a1.why: its master's implement attacks originate from its square

m4968a3.why: it rolls its own +17 vs AC and the target then takes the damage and is subject to the effects of a chosen enemy at-will melee power, off that creature's ability modifier and none of its bonuses. c.grant_row lends the whole row -- its own attack line and its own numbers -- and use() re-rolls it, so neither says this. Same sentence as m4971a3

m4969a3.why: the same borrowed at-will melee power as m4968a3, applied to a blow this row rolled. Same sentence as m4971a3

m4970a2.why: it rolls its own +19 vs AC and the target then takes the damage and is subject to the effects of a chosen enemy at-will ranged power, off that creature's ability modifier and none of its bonuses. c.grant_row lends the whole row and use() re-rolls its attack, so neither says this. Same sentence as m4968a3 and m4971a3

m4971a3.why: it chooses an at-will melee attack power belonging to an enemy it can see and, on its own attack roll, the target 'takes damage and is subject to effects as though it were hit by the chosen attack', with the damage rolled off that creature's ability modifier and none of its bonuses. c.grant_row hands over the whole row -- its own attack line, its own bonuses -- and use() re-rolls the attack, so neither says it. Nothing applies one row's Hit entry to another row's roll

m4972a3.why: the same sentence as m4971a3 for an at-will ranged attack power

m678a4.why: its whole Hit is 'the weapon used for the triggering attack drops in the target's space'; Gear holds what a creature is wielding and nothing takes it away or puts it on the floor

m709a1.why: an immediate interrupt whose whole Effect is that the conditions the triggering attack would apply land on another creature within 5 instead. c.absorb does this for damage because DamageRolled is a Decision with a mutable target; ConditionApplied and EffectApplied are notifications, so a hold can neither be refused nor re-aimed, and c.redirect moves the whole attack -- which rolls against the substitute's defence and deals it the damage too, a different sentence

m881a2.why: becomes Large and gains reach 2; Size.reach_bonus was dead code encoding a rule the game does not have, and is gone

p10145.wants: the "forced" modifier context to carry the source of the shove, or c.forced_bonus(n)
p10145.why: movement.forced reads the "forced" mods off the victim with {"how": ...} and no mention of who is shoving, so "increase the distance of any forced movement you cause by 2" cannot be gated; the row's only other clause is a skill bonus (on the causer)

p10265.why: line of sight and effect for your ranged and area powers computed from an ally. c.strike(from_=) is per-swing; nothing holds it

p10354.why: it rerolls every attack roll of one power use that missed. c.reroll_attack reaches only the one attack on c.trigger, and the earlier misses have already resolved and their bodies have already branched on them, so writing it would reroll one of several (or an event announcing a power use's finished set of attack rolls)

p10355.why: its whole Effect is taking a normal turn while stunned, dazed or unconscious and then having the condition continue. Conditions can be applied and ended and nothing can suspend one for a turn (act as though not stunned/dazed/unconscious)

p10418.why: entirely about a familiar -- teleport it, teleport to it. A familiar is a standing class feature no row creates, so c.companion() finds nothing and the row is permanently inert. Needs a familiar entity from chargen

p10420.why: same shape: entirely about a familiar that no row creates

p10424.why: take your familiar's shape -- copying another creature's speed, modes and senses. Needs c.familiar() as well

p10484.why: its whole printed Effect is 'the reach of your next melee weapon attack increases by 1'. The `reach` modifier exists but is read only by movement._threat, which is opportunity attacks; dsl.area_of takes the printed Range size and nothing else, so the row would extend what the fighter threatens and not what it can hit. Wants a reach modifier area_of consults

p10594.why: every one prints "Beast's attack bonus vs. AC" and N[B], and neither is sayable. c.companion closes none of it: a ref-less companion's Stats is a copy of its owner's, so rolling it is rolling the ranger. Needs three things -- c.b(n) alongside c.w(n) reading the companion's damage die; Attack(by='companion') rolling the companion's own bonus, since from_= moves the origin square only; and a database ref for the beast so c.call_companion(ref=) gives it numbers at all. Written with the ranger's numbers these would look finished and be wrong

p10622.why: the target regains hit points equal to half a Heal check result; the engine rolls no skill checks, so there is no number to halve

p10630.why: every one prints "Beast's attack bonus vs. AC" and N[B], and neither is sayable. c.companion closes none of it: a ref-less companion's Stats is a copy of its owner's, so rolling it is rolling the ranger. Needs three things -- c.b(n) alongside c.w(n) reading the companion's damage die; Attack(by='companion') rolling the companion's own bonus, since from_= moves the origin square only; and a database ref for the beast so c.call_companion(ref=) gives it numbers at all. Written with the ranger's numbers these would look finished and be wrong

p10702.why: its Trigger is a creature in range falling with a wall or floor within 1 square of it; falling is not modelled, so nothing announces one and there is nothing to arrest

p10705.why: 'you reduce the damage the target takes by your Dexterity modifier plus half your level'. c.absorb moves the whole amount onto the absorber and c.resist leaves a standing reduction; neither is a one-off shaving of somebody else's incoming blow

p10740.why: the whole Effect is 'until the end of the encounter your melee attacks have the rattling keyword'; the enum has no such member and nothing implements the keyword

p10744.why: a stance that doubles the normal and long range of thrown and sling attacks; Range is frozen data on the header and nothing reads a per-creature range modifier (or a Range the body can widen)

p11049.wants: a SkillCheck event to declare Trigger on
p11049.why: its whole printed trigger is 'you would make an Athletics or an Endurance check'; there are no skill checks in the engine and no event announcing one, so the row could only be declared with prose nothing reads

p11066.wants: 'reach' and 'range' read as modifiers by Power.reach_of
p11066.why: 'the target's reach increases by 1, and adds your Wisdom modifier to the range of ranged powers'. Mods.total is read for attack, damage, save, speed, forced, crit_range and defences only; reach_of never consults them

p11067.why: the whole effect is transferring 1 or 2 power points

p11101.wants: when= on c.cannot_be_flanked, the same gate c.bonus takes
p11101.why: 'neither grants combat advantage for being flanked unless both are flanked, while within 5 squares of each other'

p11168.why: 'you do not grant combat advantage to those creatures' and no -2 against their cover or concealment. ignore_cover exists only as a per-call argument to c.strike (c.no_advantage now exists, this is the other half)

p11215.why: 'use your Flurry of Blows power again'. Flurry is a class feature with no id in the spec, and nothing can re-fire a row (fire a known row now, out of turn, without spending it; plus the Flurry of Blows ref)

p11222.wants: the Flurry of Blows ref, for Trigger(PowerUsed, ...)
p11222.why: 'Trigger: you use your Flurry of Blows power'. The trigger cannot name a power that has no id

p11291.why: regain an expended Channel Divinity power. c.grant_row grants a row you do not know; this restores a spent use

p11323.why: 'resistance, but only when the damage is from ranged or area attacks'. Written ungated it would shrug off melee too, which is strictly stronger than print (the same Callable[[dict], bool] gate c.bonus takes)

p11392.why: '+10 to your initiative check'. InitiativeRolled.rolled is an int copied onto the event, so a listener setting ev.rolled is discarded; the sort re-reads the Initiative component and no Cast method writes it. init.bonus is read before the emit, so a bonus cannot reach it either. Issue #168 (change an initiative result)

p11480.wants: a long-range penalty in resolve.attack, plus c.ignores_long_range(until=)
p11480.why: 'no penalty to attack rolls for attacking at long range'. Long range is not modelled: resolve.attack never consults a weapon's ranged=(normal, long) tuple, so there is no penalty to remove and the row would be inert indistinguishably from a bug

p11603.wants: a compendium ref for the second, granted row (then c.grant_row(ref))
p11603.why: its whole Effect is 'the target can use <a second row>' -- a free-action Str-or-Dex vs Reflex 3[W] attack with its own Requirement, which the spec names only as 'p11603 Attack'. c.grant_row needs a ref and there is none; resolving the attack immediately loses the point of a daily the ally holds for later, and c.grant_attack cannot carry 3[W] vs Reflex

p11605.wants: an action point resource -- a spendable ActionPoint plus ctx['action_point'] on the attack one buys
p11605.why: its entire printed Effect is a +2 to an attack made with an action point, and nothing in the engine has an action point to spend or an event that announces one. Same gap costs clauses in p11608, p11612, p2593 and p11727

p11673.why: its printed Trigger is rolling the same number on each die of the attack roll; AttackResult keeps one face (natural) and the avenger's two-roll benefit overwrites it, so nothing can ask what the dice were. A list of every d20 face rolled for that attack makes it an ordinary AttackRolled predicate

p11725.why: 'the target repeats the attack as a free action against a creature you choose'. The reaction resolves inside the Miss window of the very use it repeats, so (actor, ref) is already in dsl._IN_FLIGHT and use refuses it. The row is otherwise complete and works when the trigger event is synthesised outside the attack's own resolution; it needs a flag exempting the granted swing from the _IN_FLIGHT guard for that one call

p11727.why: both halves are action points: the trigger is an ally missing with an action-point attack and the whole Effect is granting one that does not count against the encounter limit. Same gap as p11605

p1213.why: there is no falling and no vertical position

p12198.why: 'the attacker repeats the attack against that creature' has to fire the row that is triggering this one, and dsl._IN_FLIGHT refuses a second entry into (actor, ref) -- correctly, in general. c.redirect only works on AttackDeclared, and this triggers on a miss. Wants a way to re-run the triggering row at a new target

p12424.why: temporary hit points equal to the power points spent

p12452.why: 'shift 2 squares as a move action'. Same gap as p9430

p12500.why: every one prints "Beast's attack bonus vs. AC" and N[B], and neither is sayable. c.companion closes none of it: a ref-less companion's Stats is a copy of its owner's, so rolling it is rolling the ranger. Needs three things -- c.b(n) alongside c.w(n) reading the companion's damage die; Attack(by='companion') rolling the companion's own bonus, since from_= moves the origin square only; and a database ref for the beast so c.call_companion(ref=) gives it numbers at all. Written with the ranger's numbers these would look finished and be wrong

p12503.why: every one prints "Beast's attack bonus vs. AC" and N[B], and neither is sayable. c.companion closes none of it: a ref-less companion's Stats is a copy of its owner's, so rolling it is rolling the ranger. Needs three things -- c.b(n) alongside c.w(n) reading the companion's damage die; Attack(by='companion') rolling the companion's own bonus, since from_= moves the origin square only; and a database ref for the beast so c.call_companion(ref=) gives it numbers at all. Written with the ranger's numbers these would look finished and be wrong

p12792.wants: the class feature's id, plus c.regain(ref, *, on=)
p12792.why: 'you miss with the ranged basic attack granted by <a class feature>; you regain that power and use it immediately'. The feature has no id in the spec and nothing gives a use back

p12932.wants: on= on c.no_provoke, i.e. c.no_provoke(on=<ally>, from_=<enemy>)
p12932.why: 'cannot make opportunity attacks against any creature other than you'. The immunity can only be granted to the caster, so the row cannot loop over allies

p12945.why: 'cannot use move actions to walk or run' but may still shift. c.rooted is the exact opposite and c.immobilized also bars shifting (the mirror of c.rooted)

p12958.why: 'rolls twice when it makes a damage roll and must use the lower roll'. The damage-side counterpart of c.reroll_attack(keep='worst'). Without it the row is a 1[W] attack and nothing else

p13026.wants: c.cure(*conditions, on=) and c.immune(*conditions, until=, on=)
p13026.why: 'no longer marked or slowed, and cannot be marked or slowed until the end of your next turn'. Nothing strips a standing condition, and a mark is a Relation rather than a Condition so it needs both

p13048.why: 'cannot be slowed, immobilized, or restrained until the end of the encounter'

p13050.why: 'you are no longer surprised'. Nothing announces surprise, so the printed Trigger has nothing to name either. See #141 (and an event announcing surprise)

p13063.why: 'you can see invisible creatures and objects'

p13143.wants: a Fall event, or detail='fall' on the DamageRolled a fall produces
p13143.why: 'Trigger: you fall. Reduce falling damage by 5 + half your level.' Nothing falls -- no event, and no detail on the damage to gate on

p13314.why: 'you are not knocked prone by the triggering attack or fall'. ConditionApplied is a plain Event emitted after the condition is on you, so nothing can refuse it, and nothing models falling (or making ConditionApplied a Decision; plus a Fell event)

p13315.why: hinges on the size and kind of a teleport. MoveEnd carries kind_ but not from_; Moved carries from_/to but not kind_, so 'an ally adjacent to you before the teleport' cannot be said. One field fixes this and p13345

p13344.why: an Area wall 5. area_of knows melee, ranged, close_burst, close_blast and area_burst only, and nothing raises a multi-square barrier that blocks line of effect and can be attacked (range plus c.wall(squares, hp=, blocks_sight=) -- same as invoker p2860)

p13345.why: 'teleport the same number of squares'. Same one-field gap as p13315

p13516.wants: a carried consumable -- an object a creature holds and spends an action on
p13516.why: its whole Effect is spending a healing surge to make a seed, which lasts past the fight and which whoever carries it eats as a minor action to regain 10 + your healing surge value. Nothing here is an object a creature carries, and the heal is spent by a creature that does not own the row

p13597.why: its entire content is 'you and your allies ignore hindering and difficult terrain in the zone', plus pits inside it becoming passable. c.ignores_difficult is per-creature and board-wide, so writing it would exempt the party everywhere; without it the zone has no mechanical content at all (a zone whose squares stop counting as difficult or hindering for a named side)

p13697.why: 'squeezing does not cause you or your beast companion to take a -5 penalty, grant combat advantage, or move at half speed'. Condition.SQUEEZING exists but nothing suppresses what a condition costs while keeping the condition

p13783.why: 'does not benefit from partial cover or partial concealment on attacks made by you or allies adjacent to you'. ignore_cover= exists only per-c.strike

p13784.why: knowing an enemy's exact location and ignoring its cover/concealment for the encounter. Nothing mechanical is left over once that is gone

p13807.why: 'the target cannot become invisible to you'. Nothing can bar the HIDDEN_FROM relation being set (the inverse of c.invisible)

p13887.why: its whole Effect is making two named squares adjacent to each other, with the step between them counting as teleportation. Adjacency is computed from the grid in engine/grid.py and nothing can add an edge to it (two squares treated as adjacent for movement and melee reach)

p13925.why: its Effect raises the creature it killed onto the caster's side, dominated, at 1 hp, unable to heal. Nothing puts a dead creature back on the board or changes a creature's Team; c.summon needs a ref and spawns a fresh entity

p13984.why: BLOCKED ON CONTENT, not the engine: the creature summoned is chosen by a wizard build that does not exist, and the spec prints no stat block, so there is nothing to put in summon=. Wants chargen.BUILDS['wizard'] and a Summon per creature it can pick

p14299.wants: a weapon category -- 'simple' in Weapon.properties, or a Weapon.category field
p14299.why: Requirement is 'you must use this power with a simple weapon' and Gear/Weapon record no category, so c.wielding('simple') is false for every character in the tree: requires= would make the row permanently unusable and no requires= would let it be used with anything. Everything else on the row is sayable. Same gap makes p14301/p14302's Weapon riders inert and is why p14295/p14297 audit UNUSED

p1440.why: 'you roll initiative and dislike the result' can only be answered while initiative is being rolled, and Triggers.arm() runs *after* _roll_initiative, with encounter.order still empty -- Triggers._offer walks that order, so no creature is ever asked. Wants either arming before the roll or a Cast method that adds a flat bonus to an initiative check and re-splices

p14420.wants: the defender-aura class feature, plus c.in_my_aura(who)
p14420.why: its whole Effect is that enemies grant combat advantage while subject to your defender aura. Nothing in the tree declares that aura and c.aura only creates one; there is no way to ask who is inside it

p14428.wants: the defender-aura class feature, plus c.in_my_aura(who)
p14428.why: its printed Target is one enemy subject to your defender aura, and half its Effect pays out on an attack granted by a class feature that is not modelled. Same hold as p14420: the row could never be aimed at anything

p14508.why: you shift into an adjacent square occupied by a stone or earth object your size or larger, and nothing has line of effect to you or you to it. There are no objects, and c.hide and c.invisible are about being seen rather than about line of effect -- an attacker that knows where you are still reaches you (a state with no line of effect in either direction)

p14510.why: its Requirement and its Effect both name another druid power, which this spec gives no id for, and nothing un-spends a row: Powers.used only ever counts up (hand back a spent use)

p14548.wants: an object entity -- a targetable, movable Position with a size and no Health, reachable as a Target side
p14548.why: it targets one Medium or smaller unfastened object, animates it and slides it 5 squares a turn. Nothing in the engine is an object; Trap is the only non-creature with a Position and it is a hazard rather than scenery

p1543.why: a rift making two distant squares adjacent for movement only. Grid has no notion of a link between two squares, and neither c.teleport nor a zone can say it -- it changes what movement costs and where a creature may go, so it is not narrative

p15993.why: creates a carried object another creature expends later for healing plus a defence bonus. Nothing puts a usable object in somebody's hands; c.grant_row needs a ref that already exists and has no charges (a one-shot row handed to a creature to spend later)

p16238.wants: Wall(n, within) as a Range, or c.wall(squares, ...)
p16238.why: an area wall 5 that gives superior cover, has to be swum through, and makes whoever passes it vulnerable 5 cold. Range has kinds melee, ranged, close burst, close blast, area burst and personal, and a zone cannot say any of the three clauses

p16240.why: its whole Effect is raising or sinking a square and filling what is underneath with blocking terrain. Grid.blocking is a set nothing in Cast can add to, and there is no elevation at all

p16241.wants: a fire as a map feature, and c.terrain-style gate on one
p16241.why: the Requirement is standing next to a fire of campfire size and the destination is a square next to another one. Nothing on the board is a fire, so neither the gate nor the target can be written

p16244.wants: a fire as a map feature, with a size and a square
p16244.why: its whole Effect is expanding, extinguishing or relocating nonliving fires in a burst. Same missing thing as p16241

p16254.wants: chargen.BUILDS["warlock"] to carry an "elemental" leg, plus a named elemental affinity on the character
p16254.why: Prerequisite: Elemental Pact, and the whole row is that pact's boon -- the next enemy cursed gains vulnerable 5 to the type matching your current elemental affinity. The class has two legs, infernal and fey, so c.build cannot ask; and nothing holds an affinity for the vulnerability to name

p1926.why: the printed line is a trade: you see the invisible, and everything else goes invisible to you. The second half is writable with c.invisible(to=c.me, on=...); the first is not, because nothing overrides another effect's relation. Writing only the half that works would ship the penalty without the benefit (suppress HIDDEN_FROM towards one creature)

p2374.why: moves a live save-ends effect from one creature to another. Effects can apply and end, not move; ending and re-applying loses the effect's conditions and mods

p2389.why: its whole Effect is selecting an enemy that is taking the attack penalty from one of your rattling attacks; with no rattling there is nothing to select (to read it back)

p2633.why: 'the next melee attack you make with that weapon becomes a ranged attack with a range of 10'. Nothing re-ranges a row (or a reach override on an effect)

p2860.wants: a Wall(length, within) header range plus c.wall(...)
p2860.why: 'Area wall 5 within 10'. No wall range and no way to choose a wall's squares

p2861.why: 'each target regains a healing surge'. Writing Health.surges directly is the only route and it emits nothing, so the row audits SILENT (the counterpart of c.spend_surge)

p2870.why: 'the target does not have line of sight to any creature more than 3 squares away'. c.blinded is a different condition

p3121.why: trigger is 'you roll initiative'. InitiativeRolled *is* emitted (turns.py:128) -- the block is that its `rolled` is an int copied onto the event, so a listener changing it is discarded, and no Cast method writes the component. Issue #168 (same gap as p11392)

p3147.why: 'automatically aware of each creature within 5 squares, including hidden or invisible ones'. The inverse of c.hide/c.invisible -- c.is_hidden can ask, nothing can revoke

p32.why: there is no falling and no vertical position

p3203.why: its whole Effect is rolling damage twice and keeping the higher whenever you use an arcane power with a chosen keyword. c.maximise is a different operation and there is no reroll for damage at all

p3369.why: 'your warding provides its bonus to all your defenses, not just AC'. The row has to read the size of a standing class-feature bonus and mirror it onto Fort/Ref/Will (or c.total(what, kind=) filtered by kind)

p3397.why: a bonus to the initiative check. Initiative.bonus is read once at roll time and mods.total('initiative') is read nowhere. Issue #168 (same gap as p11392, p3331, p3121)

p3681.why: 'the target ignores the effects of the immobilized, restrained, and slowed conditions'. There is no condition immunity anywhere -- Defences.immune is damage types only -- and ConditionApplied is a notification rather than a Decision, so a row cannot refuse one either. The creature needs to keep the condition while the engine reads it as absent

p3763.wants: the dragon-magic / wild-magic fork in chargen, and c.build(...)
p3763.why: the whole Effect is changing the resistance your Dragon Soul or Wild Soul grants; chargen derives one build for this class, 'standard', so there is no resistance from a fork to change (to answer it)

p3782.why: its whole target line is one conjuration or zone and its whole Hit is destroying it. A zone is not an entity a target line can name, a conjuration has no Will to attack, and nothing ends somebody else's zone. Same missing half as the attack line of p3056 (and a way to target one)

p3838.why: entire Effect is 'move each of your zones and conjurations 5 squares'. Zones has no mover at all. The same gap silently drops the 'as a move action you can move the zone' rider from p3876, p3882, p5403 and p5404, which are written without it

p3839.why: the whole row is a *second* spirit companion. c.call_companion relocates the one you have by design and c.companion() returns one id; this needs a list, plus Range(from_='companion') and every 'adjacent to your spirit companion' reading both

p4137.why: the whole Effect is a jump of Wis squares

p4143.why: a bridge whose squares are crossed as normal terrain (a zone that makes its squares ordinary passable ground)

p4311.wants: chargen.BUILDS["warlock"] to carry a "dark" leg, and a per-character counter that survives between uses of a row
p4311.why: Prerequisite: Dark Pact. The whole row is a tally raised each time a cursed enemy drops and spent as an interrupt for 1d6 per point; nothing on a character holds a number across uses, and there is no leg to gate the prerequisite on

p4369.why: every one prints "Beast's attack bonus vs. AC" and N[B], and neither is sayable. c.companion closes none of it: a ref-less companion's Stats is a copy of its owner's, so rolling it is rolling the ranger. Needs three things -- c.b(n) alongside c.w(n) reading the companion's damage die; Attack(by='companion') rolling the companion's own bonus, since from_= moves the origin square only; and a database ref for the beast so c.call_companion(ref=) gives it numbers at all. Written with the ranger's numbers these would look finished and be wrong

p4412.why: its whole payload is an ally's attack dealing 'extra damage equal to your Hunter's Quarry damage', and that number lives in a closure inside the class feature (the dice cf:ranger-quarry pays out, readable from a row)

p4476.why: its whole Effect is 'the next ally who hits deals extra damage equal to your Sneak Attack damage'; there is no sneak attack in the model, so the row grants nothing (the class feature's dice)

p4499.why: its whole Effect is 'until the stance ends, all your attacks gain the rattling keyword'

p4562.why: 'you and one ally switch places in the initiative order; your turn ends; the ally takes its next turn immediately; you then act when your ally would have acted'. Nothing on Cast reaches Encounter.order, and c.extra_turn(at=) inserts a slot for the caster only and removes none, so half the row would be a second turn for somebody who has already had theirs

p4807.why: 'you expend an unused barbarian rage power', with the damage keyed to the expended power's level. c.forbid removes a row, which the Powers docstring says is not the same as spent. Also needs group='rage' on the rage rows: the group= header field exists and is set on nothing in the tree, so there is no queryable marker separating a rage from any other barbarian daily

p4887.why: a +4 power bonus to speed *when charging*. query.speed calls mods.total('speed') with no context, so a when= gate on a speed mod is handed {} and is false forever, and actions._charges measures speed before any charge flag exists. Ungated it would be a bonus to all movement, which is not the printed line (threading a charge key)

p5046.wants: the wild shape class feature as a row, for this one to extend
p5046.why: its whole Effect is 'until the end of the encounter you can use wild shape to assume the form of a Tiny beast'. Wild shape is not a row in this spec, so there is nothing to add a form to; the form itself is a Stealth bonus and an inability to attack, which is no reason to take it

p5051.wants: the wild shape class feature as a row, for this one to extend
p5051.why: the same sentence as p5046, for a raven with a fly speed, plus 'you can use wild shape to change among this form, another beast form and your humanoid form'. Both halves modify a row that does not exist

p5109.why: 'you and your allies have cover while within the zone'. blocks_sight is blocking terrain, not cover

p5193.wants: c.redirect accepting a resolved Hit, or c.take_hit(ev)
p5193.why: 'the triggering attack hits you instead of the ally', triggered on being hit. c.redirect works only on AttackDeclared, before the roll

p5267.why: its whole Effect is adding a number to the range of your ranged arcane powers. Nothing reads a 'range' modifier -- Power.reach.size is used raw everywhere it is used (read by dsl.candidates / Range.size)

p5275.why: its whole Effect is increasing the size of your arcane powers' blasts and bursts by 1. area_of reads Range.size raw and no modifier reaches it (read by dsl.area_of)

p5281.why: its whole Effect is 'the triggering attack also hits the target'. c.redirect moves an attack and c.autohit forces the one being answered; neither copies a resolved attack onto somebody else, and re-rolling the row would not be the same attack (apply the triggering attack to a second creature)

p5398.why: the whole Effect is ignoring cover, superior cover, concealment and total concealment against enemies in the zone. c.strike(ignore_cover=True) is per-call only

p5527.why: 'roll a d6 and add it as a power bonus to every weapon attack and damage roll'. c.bonus takes a fixed int (a modifier rolled per roll)

p5590.why: 'the ally also becomes a target of the power'. c.redirect moves the single target and cannot add one, and leaves_me_out only asks about me (on the interrupted event, plus a predicate over the attacker's own presence in ev.among)

p5591.wants: ids for the guardian form attack rows
p5591.why: c.restore_use(ref) exists but there is no ref to hand it: the guardian forms' own attacks have no ids in the spec and are not in the tree. warden/__init__.py says so and its in_form gate has no callers. Upstream of any Cast method

p5690.why: 'each target can shift as a minor action'. Nothing grants a bare action; c.grant_row grants a declared row and there is no shift row to name

p5845.why: its whole Effect is overriding the parity another row will read off its own attack roll; nothing lets one row dictate what another reads from AttackResult.natural, and the rows that read parity are the fork-gated ones

p5852.wants: action points -- a pool, a way to spend one, and an event saying so
p5852.why: the trigger is spending an action point to attack and missing. Action points are not modelled, so the trigger can never be true; warlord/level_7_b and level_9_b record the same gap

p7100.why: 'the target gains truesight 5'. The only thing the engine has for seeing the unseen is the HIDDEN_FROM relation, read at query time; there is no continuous sense to grant, and clearing the relation on whatever events happened to be watched would be an approximation

p7191.why: a bonus to the initiative check. Issue #168 (same gap as p11392, p3331, p3121)

p7192.wants: a 'blast_size' mod key read by dsl.area_of, or c.widen_areas(1, until=)
p7192.why: 'increase the size of your close blast or close burst attacks by 1'. area_of consults no modifiers

p7240.why: 'remove one condition from the target: blinded, dazed, deafened, slowed, stunned, or weakened'. Nothing takes a condition off a creature -- c.save only rolls against a save-ends effect, which is neither guaranteed nor applicable to an end-of-turn condition

p7377.wants: a spellbook -- powers a character owns but has not prepared
p7377.why: it replaces an unexpended utility or daily with another of the same level from a spellbook. Powers holds only what is known, so there is nothing to swap for and the +1 has no power to attach to

p7399.wants: a way to say an attack is made with the off-hand weapon
p7399.why: 'combat advantage for the next attack you make with an off-hand weapon'; c.w(hand='off') picks the dice but nothing marks an attack as an off-hand one, so the grant cannot be gated

p7429.why: its whole Effect is that until the end of the encounter you can cast a named at-will you already know as a minor action once per turn. c.grant_row lends a row to somebody who does not know it and changes nothing about what using it costs, and the reduced action cost is the entire row

p7639.why: 'Target: one weapon or implement', augmented for the encounter, and the wielder ends the effect on a hit as a free action. Same gap as runepriest p15993 and p9667 (plus c.give(ref, on=ally) -- a one-use row the holder spends)

p7649.why: 'Target: one weapon or implement', augmented for the encounter, and the wielder ends the effect on a hit as a free action. Same gap as runepriest p15993 and p9667 (plus c.give(ref, on=ally) -- a one-use row the holder spends)

p924.why: Condition.SURPRISED is in the enum and nothing ever applies it

p9430.why: 'until the stance ends you can shift 1 square as a minor action'. actions.legal hardcodes a one-square shift at move cost and nothing reads a shift-cost modifier (or a 'shift' key honoured by actions.legal)

p9438.why: Area wall 5 within 10, blocking sight for everyone but the caster (header range plus except_= on blocks_sight -- same wall gap as p2860, p13344)

p9442.why: entirely 'damage from your assassin's shroud', per shroud. Shrouds have no representation anywhere; shroud riders were also dropped from six written rows (> int, c.shroud(on=, n=1), and a shroud-damage event)

p9665.why: commands a summoned creature to use its instinctive effect. Needs Summon.instinctive -- a callable the block carries

p9667.wants: a carried consumable -- an object a creature holds and spends an action on
p9667.why: four berries, each consumed as a minor action for 10 hit points, a saving throw, or 10 temporary hit points. Same missing thing as p13516

p9818.wants: keep= on c.strike/c.attack, and both results readable off AttackResult
p9818.why: 'make the attack roll twice and use either result', with a deeper penalty if both would hit. c.reroll_attack has keep=; the first roll does not
